Evidence: Menexenus 242e-243a [obs_menexenus_0064]. Its function is performance-setup; funeral oration deeds catalogue instead has a performance-setup function.

dispositions.label: war_cause_attributed_to_jealousy
dispositions.reason: Menexenus attributes war to jealousy, giving an erotic motive to collective violence rather than treating conflict as an impersonal accident. Evidence: Menexenus 242a-242b [obs_menexenus_0054]. Its function is dramatic-setup; civil war attributed to misfortune instead has a dramatic-setup function.

dispositions.label: war_ethic_doublestandard_kinsman_vs_barbarian
dispositions.reason: Menexenus contrasts treatment of kinsmen with treatment of barbarians, exposing a double standard in the city’s war ethic. Evidence: Menexenus 242c-242d [obs_menexenus_0055]; Menexenus 244b-244c [obs_menexenus_0063]. Its function is dramatic-setup; war cause attributed to jealousy instead has a local function.

dispositions.label: water_source_description
dispositions.reason: Critias describes the water source that sustains the settlement, making a physical feature carry the city’s material and spatial history. Evidence: Critias 116e-117a [obs_critias_0072]. Its function is dramatic-setup; collective interest as norm source instead has a dramatic-setup function.

dispositions.label: whole_city_self_charm
dispositions.reason: Laws presents the city as charming itself through shared song and civic pleasure, making collective self-enchantment a regime-design instrument. Evidence: Laws 665c-665d [obs_laws_0214]. Its function is regime-design; sophist self advertisement instead has a dramatic-setup function.

dispositions.label: wine_test_as_diagnostic_method
dispositions.reason: Laws uses the wine test diagnostically: controlled intoxication reveals character and trains judgment, so pleasure becomes a method of civic inquiry. Evidence: Laws 649d [obs_laws_0356]. Its function is cultural-test; autobiographical method announced instead has a narrative-return function.

dispositions.label: apparent_contradiction_distinguished_by_respect
dispositions.reason: At Sophist 255d–256a, the Stranger assigns motion both being and otherness while denying that it is rest; the apparent contradiction is resolved by changing the respect of predication. This is narrower than the adjacent perceptual-contradiction cluster, where opposed sensible appearances drive inquiry toward an essence, so the two comparison questions should remain separate (obs_sophist_0322, 255d-256a).

dispositions.label: appearance_reality_distinction
dispositions.reason: Shared textual function: both the source and target record an appearance/reality contrast that tests seeming presentation against what is genuinely the case; local objects and argumentative settings remain in the observations. Complete source membership (1 records) and target membership (7 records) were reviewed. Comparison question: How does the appearance/reality contrast test or reorganize the claim under examination?

dispositions.label: appearance_vs_reality_construal
dispositions.reason: Across Gorgias 463e–464a, Parmenides 164d–164e, Philebus 42b–42c, Republic 515c–515d, and Sophist 240a–240b, the passages repeatedly make a seeming presentation answer to a different standard—condition, magnitude, release, or being—rather than simply naming an image. The neighboring image/truth cluster tests representations or seeming goods for deficiency against truth; these memberships also stage perspectival and ontological re-description, so that narrower question is not enough (obs_gorgias_0049, 463e-464a; obs_parmenides_0214, 164d-164e; obs_philebus_0176, 42b-42c; obs_republic_0732, 515c-515d; obs_sophist_0136, 240a-240b).

dispositions.label: ascent_culmination
dispositions.reason: Symposium 211a–212a is a terminal sequence: after the ascent, Diotima marks the vision of Beauty as the point at which life is worth living and truth is encountered. The nearby ascent-stage material at 210a–210b moves the lover from bodies to souls; it describes progression, not the endpoint, so merging would erase the structural stage boundary (obs_symposium_0143, 211a-211b; obs_symposium_0145, 211c-211e; obs_symposium_0155, 212a).

dispositions.label: beauty_ascent_stage_transition
dispositions.reason: At Symposium 210a–210b, the two memberships track the lover's movement from recognizing one beauty across bodies to turning toward beauty in souls. That transition is adjacent to the later vision-and-life endpoint, but it is a change of object in the ascent rather than its culmination; the stage boundary is distinct (obs_symposium_0138, 210a-210b; obs_symposium_0139, 210a-210b).

dispositions.label: beauty_visible_in_earthly_likenesses
dispositions.reason: Phaedrus 250a–250b singles out beauty as the Form that remained visibly bright in the prenatal vision, making earthly beauty the perceptible trigger or trace of a prior vision. The general visible/intelligible cluster maps two domains or cognitive routes; this membership instead explains a privileged manifestation of beauty, so the functions should not be merged (obs_phaedrus_0157, 250a-250b).

dispositions.label: being_as_one_form_among_others
dispositions.reason: Sophist 256e–257a places Being among the kinds and says it is other than the other kinds, treating Being as one member within an articulated field. The nearby exclusivity argument makes the One the sole bearer of being-one; the taxonomy of kinds has a distinct function from the operation that limits formal identity (obs_sophist_0213, 256e-257a).

dispositions.label: being_as_third_thing_beyond_opposites
dispositions.reason: At Sophist 250a–250d, Being is introduced as something other than the pair of motion and rest, a third term required by the deduction. The later 254c–254d cluster asks how Being mixes with both kinds while they remain unmixed with one another; adding a term and specifying its relations are distinct steps (obs_sophist_0178, 250a-250b; obs_sophist_0189, 250c-250d).

dispositions.label: being_becoming_contrast
dispositions.reason: Republic 485a–486b uses the being/becoming opposition to identify what philosophic natures desire: stable essence rather than generated things. The adjacent directional cluster follows how study or soul turns from becoming toward being; this passage supplies the object of desire, not a trajectory of inquiry (obs_republic_0804, 485a-486b).

dispositions.label: being_becoming_distinction_with_epistemic_correlates
dispositions.reason: Philebus 53c–53d, 59a–59b, 61e–62a, and Timaeus 27d–28a pair the being/becoming distinction with classifications of pleasure, opinion, knowledge, and cosmological inquiry. Unlike a bare being-versus-becoming contrast, these passages align ontological status with an epistemic or affective correlate; that cross-domain pairing is a distinct reason to keep it separate (obs_philebus_0269, 53c-53d; obs_philebus_0299, 59a-59b; obs_philebus_0340, 61e-62a; obs_timaeus_0072, 27d-28a).

dispositions.label: being_becoming_orientation
dispositions.reason: Parmenides 154b–154c, Republic 521d–522b and 526c–527a, and Timaeus 28b–28c use being/becoming as a direction, temporal orientation, or movement of thought from one register to another. The neighboring contrast cluster states the opposition as an object of preference or classification; these memberships instead track where an inquiry or account is headed (obs_parmenides_0181, 154b-154c; obs_republic_0312, 526c-527a; obs_republic_0813, 521d-522b; obs_timaeus_0065, 28b-28c).

dispositions.label: being_defined_as_body_or_contact
dispositions.reason: Sophist 246a–246c reports the materialist thesis that being is body, defined by contact or impact. The adjacent form/sensible comparisons ask how intelligible realities differ from perceptible instances; they do not define being by a bodily criterion, so the evidential operation is distinct in structure (obs_sophist_0318, 246a-246c).

dispositions.label: being_mixed_with_both_rest_and_motion
dispositions.reason: Sophist 254c–254d asserts that Being mixes with both Rest and Motion while Rest and Motion do not mix with each other, a one-way relation among kinds. The earlier third-term argument at 250c–250d establishes Being as distinct from the pair; it does not perform this later mixing test (obs_sophist_0205, 254c-254d).

dispositions.label: beings_by_themselves_vs_relative
dispositions.reason: Sophist 255b–255c distinguishes things said by themselves from things said only in relation to another, setting a grammatical and ontological frame for predication. The nearest relative-property material asks whether a shape is beautiful in itself or relative to something; this passage's function is to classify modes of saying rather than evaluate a property (obs_sophist_0209, 255b-255c).

dispositions.label: body_impediment_catalog
dispositions.reason: Six Phaedo memberships (66b–66e, 79c–79d, 82d–83b, and 95c–95d) together with Timaeus 43b–43c accumulate bodily impediments: appetite, acquisition, perception, imprisonment, disorder, and destructive motion all obstruct the soul. The sensory-route cluster isolates the epistemic failure of relying on perception; this broader catalog includes bodily and practical burdens, so its comparison boundary should remain (obs_phaedo_0043, 66b-66c; obs_phaedo_0044, 66d-66e; obs_phaedo_0104, 79c-79d; obs_phaedo_0116, 82d-82e; obs_phaedo_0119, 83a-83b; obs_phaedo_0170, 95c-95d; obs_timaeus_0124, 43b-43c).

dispositions.label: body_part_near_immortality_asserted
dispositions.reason: At Phaedo 80d–80e, Cebes tests the mortality argument by asking whether bones and sinews might be quasi-immortal even as bodies decay. This is a counterexample about bodily persistence, not the catalog of ways embodiment impedes inquiry; the adjacent impediment cluster therefore cannot absorb it (obs_phaedo_0108, 80d-80e).

dispositions.label: causal_property_by_which_x_is_x
dispositions.reason: Greater Hippias 294a–294b uses the exceeding as a proposed cause by which large things—and by analogy beautiful things—are what they are. The nearby essence/property comparison at 302a–302c examines whether a predicate is intrinsic or relative; causal explanation and property classification are different operations (obs_greater-hippias_0076, 294a-294b).

dispositions.label: city_soul_isomorphism_asserted
dispositions.reason: Republic 435a–435b and 440c–442a explicitly assert structural correspondence between city and soul, including the same kinds and the form of justice. The adjacent city-to-soul predicate-transfer cluster applies civic predicates to a soul; it is an analogical projection, not the stronger isomorphism claim recorded here (obs_republic_0137, 435a-435b; obs_republic_0142, 440c-442a).

dispositions.label: city_soul_isomorphism_claim
dispositions.reason: Shared textual function: the city and soul are asserted to share an isomorphic structure for parallel predication or explanation. Passage-specific details remain in the observation fields. Complete source membership (1 records) and target membership (2 records) were reviewed. Comparison question: How does the argument assert structural correspondence between city and soul?

dispositions.label: city_soul_parallel_predication
dispositions.reason: Republic 577e–578d transfers the tyrannized city's poverty and condition to the tyrannical soul and man, using one domain to predicate the other. The neighboring isomorphism cluster asserts shared internal structure; this passage performs a cross-domain analogy without establishing identity, so it remains distinct (obs_republic_0828, 577e-578d).

dispositions.label: contrasting_soul_portrait
dispositions.reason: Phaedo 81a–81d and 108a–108b present contrasting postmortem soul portraits: stained souls become phantoms, while orderly souls follow their proper route. The adjacent soul-visibility material asks how to inspect the soul's true nature once bodily accretions are removed; postmortem characterization and epistemic disclosure are not one function (obs_phaedo_0110, 81a-81b; obs_phaedo_0112, 81c-81d; obs_phaedo_0223, 108a-108b).

dispositions.label: cosmos_as_image_of_paradigm
dispositions.reason: Shared textual function: the visible cosmos is related as an image or likeness to an intelligible living paradigm. Passage-specific details remain in the observation fields. Complete source membership (1 records) and target membership (1 records) were reviewed. Comparison question: How does the cosmos receive intelligible structure by relation to its paradigm?

dispositions.label: curriculum_prelude_to_dialectic
dispositions.reason: Republic 531d–532d calls the preceding mathematical studies preludes that prepare the soul for dialectic. This curricular framing is adjacent to the dialectical ascent cluster, which describes the actual noetic movement through Forms and toward understanding; preparation and ascent should not be collapsed (obs_republic_0819, 531d-532d).

dispositions.label: deictic_naming_denied_to_changing_things
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 49d denies stable deictic naming to elemental appearances because each changes and cannot remain the same thing. The neighboring receptacle rule positively reserves deictic reference for the underlying field; withholding a demonstrative from changeable qualities is a structurally distinct linguistic operation (obs_timaeus_0181, 49d).

dispositions.label: deictic_naming_reserved_for_receptacle
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 49e–50a reserves deictic naming for the receptacle that remains while generated qualities change. The adjacent receiver-naming material identifies the receptacle's role as nurse or receiver; the former is a distinct criterion for reference, the latter an ontological description (obs_timaeus_0182, 49e-50a).

dispositions.label: dependence_of_lower_on_higher
dispositions.reason: Laws 631b–631c depicts human goods as hanging from or depending on divine goods, making a vertical dependence claim between levels of value. The stable-being hierarchy cluster orders things by permanence or participation in being; it does not express this asymmetric dependence, so the evidence supports a separate label (obs_laws_0044, 631b-631c).

dispositions.label: dialectic_noetic_ascent
dispositions.reason: Republic 511c, 533d, 534e, and 536d–537c describe dialectic as a no-sense route through Forms, a drawing-up of the soul, a synopsis of studies, and the culminating training of the philosopher. The nearby necessity cluster states what Forms make discourse possible; these memberships instead track the active ascent and completion of a knower (obs_republic_0273, 511c; obs_republic_0330, 533d; obs_republic_0346, 534e; obs_republic_0353, 536d-537c).

dispositions.label: divided_line_cognitive_mapping
dispositions.reason: Republic 476e–478c, 511d (both memberships), and 533d map objects and cognitive states across the divided line, including the relation of hypotheses to intelligible understanding. The intelligible/visible distinction cluster states the two-domain contrast itself; this set supplies an ordered cognitive map and transitions among its levels (obs_republic_0174, 476e-478c; obs_republic_0276, 511d; obs_republic_0277, 511d; obs_republic_0329, 533d).

dispositions.label: divine_as_paradigm
dispositions.reason: Phaedrus 253a, 253b–253c, and Republic 500c make divine likeness a standard for ordering the lover or guardian's life and work. The neighboring paradigm-standard cluster uses formal models to shape names, cities, or cosmos; assimilation to a divine exemplar is an ethical and psychagogic operation, not generic model construction (obs_phaedrus_0316, 253a; obs_phaedrus_0166, 253b-253c; obs_republic_0728, 500c).

dispositions.label: eide_in_stoicheia
dispositions.reason: Cratylus 424d–424e asks whether realities themselves contain eide corresponding to the phonetic elements used in names. The nearby craft-production use of eidos directs a name-maker to a form as a model; this membership tests the structural units of reality and language rather than a maker's procedure (obs_cratylus_0201, 424d-424e).

dispositions.label: eidos_applied_to_conceptual_kinds
dispositions.reason: Theaetetus 181c–181d applies eidos language to distinguish kinds of motion, such as alteration and locomotion, within a conceptual classification. The greatest-kinds framework invokes an already agreed ontological set for deductions; classifying motion types here is a narrower sorting function, so the evidence does not support merging (obs_theaetetus_0228, 181c-181d).

dispositions.label: eidos_in_craft_production
dispositions.reason: Cratylus 390d–390e makes the name-giver look to the form or nature of a name in carrying out the craft of naming. A broader model-standard cluster compares exemplars used to make or judge things across domains; this is specifically a production procedure grounded in a craft analogy (obs_cratylus_0043, 390d-390e).

dispositions.label: elemental_appearance_as_receiver_condition
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 51b explains elemental names as conditions received in the receptacle—fiery, moist, and so on—rather than as independently stable things. The adjacent deictic rule concerns which underlying thing may be called this; this passage interprets names through received appearances, so the operations are structurally distinct and not interchangeable (obs_timaeus_0189, 51b).

dispositions.label: elemental_identity_problem_raised
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 49b raises the prior identity puzzle: if elemental appearances continually change, it is hard to say what each element stably is. The neighboring threefold-generation schema supplies a settled model of Form, copy, and receptacle; this membership records the unresolved problem that motivates clarification, not the completed schema; the unresolved problem is structurally distinct (obs_timaeus_0179, 49b).

dispositions.label: embodied_soul_initial_mindlessness
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 44a–44b describes the soul as initially mindless when bound into a mortal body, then gradually acquiring intelligence through growth and nourishment. The adjacent soul-portrait cluster compares differentiated conditions or fates of souls; this is a developmental account of embodied cognition, not a portrait contrast (obs_timaeus_0130, 44a-44b).

dispositions.label: eristic_dialectic_contrast_via_eide
dispositions.reason: Philebus 16e–17a and Republic 453b–454e contrast ordered collection and division through Forms with eristic or antilogic that rushes from one to many and obscures distinctions. The one-over-many reasoning cluster performs the reusable method on particular arguments; these memberships instead diagnose competing dialectical procedures, so the methodological contrast should remain separate (obs_philebus_0039, 16e-17a; obs_republic_0149, 453b-454e).

dispositions.label: essence_convention_contrast
dispositions.reason: Theaetetus 171e–172b sets convention and social decree against an independent nature in claims about just, unjust, holy, and unholy. The neighboring essence/property cluster examines whether a quality belongs intrinsically or relatively; convention versus nature is a source-of-norm dispute, not a property test (obs_theaetetus_0414, 171e-172b).

dispositions.label: essence_property_contrast
dispositions.reason: Greater Hippias 302a–302c uses the both/each distinction to ask whether pleasures through sight and hearing are beautiful in themselves or in relation to something. The nearby exceeding account proposes what causes a thing to be beautiful or large; testing intrinsic versus relative predication is a distinct argumentative operation (obs_greater-hippias_0170, 302a-302c).

dispositions.label: form_account_deferred_to_image
dispositions.reason: Republic 506a–507a is a controlled deferral: Socrates withholds a direct account of the Good and substitutes an offspring-and-payment image. The adjacent image/truth cluster evaluates representations or seeming goods against truth; this passage manages the terms of exposition rather than claiming that its metaphor is a deficient copy (obs_republic_0812, 506a-507a).

dispositions.label: form_being_exclusive_to_form
dispositions.reason: Parmenides 157e–158a restricts the predicate being-one to the One itself while treating the others as participating in it, preserving an exclusivity within the deduction. The adjacent Sophist taxonomy places Being among many kinds; formal exclusivity and kind-membership answer distinct questions (obs_parmenides_0187, 157e-158a).

dispositions.label: form_existence_alternative_raised
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 51c frames a choice between intelligible Forms as true realities and bodily perceptibles as the only things some might call true. The paradigm-standard cluster asks how a model guides production or judgment; this membership stages an existence alternative before any paradigm is applied (obs_timaeus_0190, 51c).

dispositions.label: form_identified_as_what_thing_is
dispositions.reason: Cratylus 389b–389c identifies a tool's form with what that tool truly is, using the shuttle as the example. The adjacent craft-production membership asks how a maker looks to a form while making a name; identifying essence and describing production are distinct operations (obs_cratylus_0036, 389b-389c).

dispositions.label: form_name_extension
dispositions.reason: Phaedo 103d–106b extends the naming rule from a Form to non-Form bearers: numbers, opposite-bearing things, soul, life, and the immortal inherit or exclude predicates through the relevant Form. The form-object cluster introduces or names Forms themselves; these six memberships instead track how a Form's name and opposite-exclusion rule propagate to participants (obs_phaedo_0210, 103d-103e; obs_phaedo_0211, 104a-104b; obs_phaedo_0212, 104c-104d; obs_phaedo_0214, 105b-105c; obs_phaedo_0216, 105d-105e; obs_phaedo_0217, 106a-106b).

dispositions.label: form_object_introduced
dispositions.reason: Across Parmenides 130a–131a, 130e–131a, 134e–135a, 149e–150a; Phaedo 65c–65d, 73e–74a, 75c–75d, 76d–76e, 100b–100c, 106c–106d; Philebus 57e–58a; and Sophist 225c–225d, the text repeatedly posits Forms as self-predicative objects, kinds, opposites, or objects of precise knowledge. The adjacent property-catalogue cluster deduces what already posited Forms can be or do; this set records introduction and identification, not the later inventory of properties (obs_parmenides_0026, 130a-130b; obs_parmenides_0041, 130e-131a; obs_parmenides_0054, 134e-135a; obs_parmenides_0145, 149e-150a; obs_phaedo_0040, 65c-65d; obs_phaedo_0078, 73e-74a; obs_phaedo_0084, 75c-75d; obs_phaedo_0090, 76d-76e; obs_phaedo_0192, 100b-100c; obs_phaedo_0218, 106c-106d; obs_philebus_0310, 57e-58a; obs_sophist_0051, 225c-225d).

dispositions.label: form_of_good_as_cause_and_paradigm
dispositions.reason: Republic 505a, 508d–509b, 517c–518b, and 540a–540e give the Good causal and paradigmatic reach: it makes things useful, supplies truth and knowledge, illuminates rightness, and directs the rulers. The neighboring generic paradigm cluster treats a model as a standard for names, cities, or cosmos; the Good's causal status and beyond-being role make this a distinct operation (obs_republic_0237, 505a; obs_republic_0259, 508d-509b; obs_republic_0292, 517c-518b; obs_republic_0364, 540a-540e).

dispositions.label: form_of_good_dialectical_test
dispositions.reason: Republic 534b and 534c make knowledge of the Good answerable to an account: failure to distinguish and explain it leaves the speaker at the level of image or opinion. The neighboring Good cluster describes what the Good causes or illuminates; this pair tests dialectical competence rather than ontological function (obs_republic_0339, 534b; obs_republic_0340, 534c).

dispositions.label: form_paradigm_standard
dispositions.reason: Across Cratylus 389d–390a, Republic 471b–472e, 500d–501c, 592b, and Timaeus 39d–39e, a paradigm or standard is used to construct, assess, or orient a name, city, ruler, or cosmos. The adjacent Good cluster attributes causal and epistemic power specifically to the Good; these memberships instead compare the reusable model-setting operation across domains (obs_cratylus_0037, 389d-390a; obs_republic_0169, 471b-472e; obs_republic_0216, 500d-501c; obs_republic_0533, 592b; obs_timaeus_0113, 39d-39e).

dispositions.label: form_properties_catalogue
dispositions.reason: Parmenides 134a–134b, 139d–139e, 141d, and 144e–145a; Phaedo 78d–78e; Philebus 59c–59d; and Symposium 211a–211b accumulate formal properties—knowledge, sameness and difference, temporal predicates, numerical multiplicity, stability, and Beauty's negative predicates. The neighboring form-object cluster introduces entities such as the Equal Itself or Beauty Itself; this set performs a property inventory and deduction about already introduced objects (obs_parmenides_0063, 134a-134b; obs_parmenides_0086, 139d-139e; obs_parmenides_0092, 141d; obs_parmenides_0113, 144e-145a; obs_phaedo_0101, 78d-78e; obs_philebus_0291, 59c-59d; obs_symposium_0141, 211a-211b).

dispositions.label: form_request
dispositions.reason: Across Euthyphro 6d–6e and 11a–11b, Greater Hippias 288a–288b and 289d–289e, Meno 72c–73c, and Philebus 63e–64a, the speaker repeatedly asks for the Form or what-it-is rather than an example, property, or list. By contrast, the nearby form-introduction group records a Form appearing as an object of discourse; these memberships record the distinct interlocutor's demand that such an account be supplied (obs_euthyphro_0010, 6d-6e; obs_euthyphro_0018, 11a-11b; obs_greater-hippias_0047, 288a-288b; obs_greater-hippias_0055, 289d-289e; obs_meno_0008, 72c-73c; obs_philebus_0315, 63e-64a).

dispositions.label: form_sensible_contrast
dispositions.reason: Across Euthydemus 300e–301a; Parmenides 135d–135e; Phaedo 74b–74c, 74d–74e, and 78d–78e; Phaedrus 250c–250d; Republic 478d–484a and 529c–529d; Statesman 285e–286a; and Timaeus 28b–28c, sensible cases are tested against Forms or intelligible standards, often exposing likeness, instability, or inferiority. The intelligible/visible cluster simply separates realms or modes of cognition; this cluster performs a comparative test of sensible adequacy, so its evidence should remain distinct (obs_euthydemus_0179, 300e-301a; obs_parmenides_0061, 135d-135e; obs_phaedo_0079, 74b-74c; obs_phaedo_0080, 74d-74e; obs_phaedo_0102, 78d-78e; obs_phaedrus_0147, 250c-250d; obs_republic_0176, 478d-484a; obs_republic_0320, 529c-529d; obs_statesman_0177, 285e; obs_statesman_0178, 286a; obs_timaeus_0066, 28b-28c).

dispositions.label: form_vocabulary_in_dialectical_classification
dispositions.reason: Sophist 254a–254b identifies the philosopher by attachment to the Form of what is through reasoning, in contrast with the sophist's obscurity. The nearby mythic form-language cluster embeds beauty/Form vocabulary in a narrated palinode; dialectical classification and mythic deployment are different textual settings and operations (obs_sophist_0188, 254a-254b).

dispositions.label: form_vocabulary_in_myth
dispositions.reason: Phaedrus 250e–251a places beauty/Form language inside the palinode's myth to connect the beloved's visible face with its Form. The adjacent supercelestial-vision cluster records where Forms are seen, while this membership marks how myth carries the vocabulary; location and rhetorical deployment should not merge (obs_phaedrus_0150, 250e-251a).

dispositions.label: forms_as_thought_proposal
dispositions.reason: Parmenides 132b–132c proposes that a Form could be a thought in a soul, a hypothesis intended to avoid the regress caused by separate Forms. The adjacent self-relation cluster interrogates relations among Forms themselves; a proposed explanatory model and a self-reference problem are not the same argumentative move (obs_parmenides_0047, 132b-132c).

dispositions.label: forms_for_trivial_things_rejected
dispositions.reason: At Parmenides 130c–130d, Socrates hesitates to posit Forms for hair, mud, and dirt, marking a boundary around what the theory can intelligibly treat as a Form. The nearby audience-rejection case asks whether ordinary people accept the Beautiful Itself; scope of ontology and refusal by an audience are structurally distinct pressures (obs_parmenides_0021, 130c-130d).

dispositions.label: forms_inferred_from_intellect_opinion_difference
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 51d infers separate, imperceptible Forms from the distinction between intellect and true opinion, using a difference in cognition as an ontological criterion. The neighboring knowledge/opinion comparison sorts epistemic states by origin, account, and stability; this passage instead reasons from that contrast to the existence of its objects (obs_timaeus_0191, 51d).

dispositions.label: forms_interrelate_mutually
dispositions.reason: Parmenides 133c–133d and 150c make Forms what they are through relations among Forms, including the exclusive contrast between Largeness Itself and Smallness Itself. The adjacent discourse cluster asks how Forms combine so that logos is possible; mutual constitution is not the same textual move as interweaving for speech (obs_parmenides_0051, 133c-133d; obs_parmenides_0155, 150c).

dispositions.label: forms_interweaving_enables_logos
dispositions.reason: Sophist 259d–259e argues that separating each thing from every other destroys logos, so discourse requires Forms to interweave. The nearby precondition argument says that rejecting Forms makes thought and dialectic impossible; this membership identifies the positive combinatorial function of speech rather than the necessity of Forms as such (obs_sophist_0246, 259d-259e).

dispositions.label: forms_necessary_for_dialectic
dispositions.reason: The Parmenides argument at 135b–135c says that without a Form for each thing, thought and dialectic would have no object or distinction to work with. The neighboring ascent material describes a knower moving through Forms; this is a structural condition that makes dialectic possible, not the later method or ascent itself (obs_parmenides_0056, 135b-135c).

dispositions.label: forms_seen_in_supercelestial_place
dispositions.reason: In Phaedrus 247d–247e, the soul following a god beholds justice itself, temperance itself, and knowledge in the hyperouranian region. dispositions.label: forms_self_referential_relation

dispositions.label: forms_separate_from_us

dispositions.label: forms_undergoing_opposites_would_be_astonishing

dispositions.label: hypothesis_without_first_principle

dispositions.label: intrinsic_vs_relative_property_contrast

dispositions.label: knowledge_death_condition
dispositions.reason: The accepted Phaedo memberships at 66d–66e and 67e–68a make release from the body a condition for pure knowledge, while the Parmenides membership at 134c–134d is a rejected repair about separated human and divine knowledge rather than that condition. dispositions.label: knowledge_requires_grasp_of_being
dispositions.reason: Theaetetus 186b–186c makes attaining truth depend on attaining being, so a failure to grasp what something is blocks knowledge rather than merely producing an incomplete opinion. The neighboring knowledge/opinion comparison distinguishes epistemic statuses by their sources and stability; this membership states an ontological prerequisite for knowing (obs_theaetetus_0272, 186b-186c).

dispositions.label: knowledge_vs_right_opinion
dispositions.reason: Meno 98a–99a contrasts true opinion with knowledge through teachability and the need for an explanatory account, while Timaeus 51e contrasts intellect and true opinion by origin, account, stability, and distribution. The adjacent grasp-of-being claim makes being a condition of truth and knowledge; these memberships function as a comparison between two epistemic states and their grounds (obs_meno_0041, 98a-99a; obs_timaeus_0192, 51e).

dispositions.label: koina_terms_catalog
dispositions.reason: Theaetetus 185c–185d catalogs the common terms—being and not-being, likeness and unlikeness, sameness and difference, unity and number—that the soul considers beyond any single sense. dispositions.label: longer_road_methodological_hedge
dispositions.reason: Republic 435c–435e says the exact relation between the city's and soul's three Forms cannot yet be answered and requires a longer road. dispositions.label: many_reject_forms
dispositions.reason: Republic 493c–494b asks whether the many would accept the Beautiful Itself and each thing itself rather than the many beautiful things and ordinary individuals. dispositions.label: name_reality_contrast
dispositions.reason: Laws 626a–626b contrasts what people call peace with the war that exists in deed, while Parmenides 147d–147e tests a name against the nature to which it refers. dispositions.label: naming_gap_in_negations
dispositions.reason: Sophist 257d–257e pauses over whether the part of the Different opposed to the beautiful has a name at all. dispositions.label: negation_as_otherness_part
dispositions.reason: At Sophist 257d–257e, the Stranger treats not-beautiful as a subdivision within the nature of the Different rather than as privation or sheer non-being. dispositions.reason: The Sophist deductions at 258a–258b and 258c–258d identify not-being with otherness rather than contrariety and count that nature as one form among beings. dispositions.label: not_being_as_unlimited_multitude
dispositions.reason: Sophist 256e–257a says that relative to each Form, being is many while not-being is unlimited in multitude. dispositions.label: not_being_necessity_claim
dispositions.reason: At Sophist 256d, the Stranger concludes that not-being exists of necessity through the nature of the Other, both for motion and across the kinds. dispositions.label: perception_summons_intellection
dispositions.reason: Three accepted Republic passages and a rejected Theaetetus repair converge on the trigger: a perception that reports contrary or unresolved features forces the soul to ask what the thing is, while ordinary single reports do not. dispositions.label: philosophical_nature_conditional_development

dispositions.label: physical_recoil_at_form_vision

The bodily reaction has a structural difference from the nearby claim that sensible beauty awakens memory of Beauty itself (obs_phaedrus_0180, 254a-254b).

dispositions.label: popular_vs_refined_conceptions_of_the_good
dispositions.reason: Republic 505b sets the many's identification of the good with pleasure against a more refined identification with understanding, making disagreement over the good's content part of the argument. dispositions.label: possibility_admission_with_difficulty

dispositions.label: prenatal_knowledge_inferred
dispositions.reason: The Meno and four Phaedo passages use untaught correct answers, recollection, and the Equal Itself to infer knowledge acquired before bodily perception. The inferential function is temporal priority of knowledge, distinct from the neighboring contrast that separates knowledge from right opinion by account or teachability (obs_meno_0023, 85b-86b; obs_phaedo_0072, 73a-73b; obs_phaedo_0081, 74d-74e; obs_phaedo_0082, 75a-75b; obs_phaedo_0083, 75a-75b).

dispositions.label: primary_vs_eidolon_distinction
dispositions.reason: Lysis 219d–219e distinguishes the first object loved for its own sake from secondary objects called friends because they lead toward it, giving primary and derivative referents different explanatory roles. That hierarchy is distinct from image-versus-truth comparisons, where an eidolon is measured against its original rather than ordered by teleological priority (obs_lysis_0117, 219d-219e).

dispositions.label: pterosis_graded_by_character
dispositions.reason: Two Phaedrus 256 passages grade the soul's wing-growth and afterlife by whether lovers yield to bodily desire or master it, linking degree of winging to character. The ethical scale creates a structural separation from the adjacent wing-sprout imagery, which follows the metaphor's physiological growth without making character the measure (obs_phaedrus_0173, 256c-256d; obs_phaedrus_0318, 256b).

dispositions.label: pure_intellect_method
dispositions.reason: Three Phaedo passages prescribe turning to thought alone, guarding the soul's purity, and trusting what it itself understands rather than the senses. This is a positive method for securing intelligible objects, structurally distinct from the negative claim that sensory routes cannot yield truth (obs_phaedo_0042, 65e-66a; obs_phaedo_0046, 67a-67b; obs_phaedo_0118, 83a-83b).

dispositions.label: rational_irrational_contrast
dispositions.reason: Republic 546c uses rational and irrational diameters to mark a numerical difference in the city's generative calculation, not a generic opposition between reason and appetite. The mathematical function is distinct from being-and-becoming contrasts, which sort ontological status rather than geometrical number (obs_republic_0380, 546c).

dispositions.label: receiver_must_lack_received_forms
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 50e–51a argues that the receptacle must lack a fixed form so it can receive all forms without privileging one, using neutral material analogies to constrain its nature. This receiver-condition is distinct from the passage that first names the receptacle as the place and nurse of generation (obs_timaeus_0187, 50e; obs_timaeus_0188, 51a).

This provisional naming has a distinct function from the argument that a receiver must be formless to take in every shape (obs_timaeus_0178, 49a).

dispositions.label: reciprocal_epistemic_isolation
dispositions.reason: Parmenides 134d–135a derives a reciprocal knowledge barrier from separation: human knowledge cannot reach divine Forms and divine knowledge cannot be directed at human affairs. This relational isolation is a distinct two-way epistemic consequence, not the Phaedo's claim that bodily release is a condition for pure knowledge (obs_parmenides_0053, 134d-135a).

dispositions.label: recollection_rarity_and_forgetfulness
dispositions.reason: Phaedrus 250a–250b ranks souls by how much of the supercelestial vision they remember, with only a few retaining enough to recognize what they see and most forgetting. The membership's function is distribution and loss of recollection, distinct from the later trigger in which a beloved face revives memory (obs_phaedrus_0155, 250a-250b).

dispositions.label: recollection_triggered_by_sensible_beauty
dispositions.reason: Phaedrus 254a–254b shows the beloved's face and beauty stirring the charioteer's memory of Beauty itself, so sensible appearance acts as an occasion for recollection rather than its source. That trigger mechanism is distinct from the rarity-and-forgetfulness scale that classifies souls by retained vision (obs_phaedrus_0179, 254a-254b).

dispositions.label: relational_being_necessity
dispositions.reason: Theaetetus 160b–160c makes a sensible quality exist only in relation to a perceiver, so becoming sweet or bitter is indexed to someone's experience. This relational ontology is distinct from the Sophist's necessity claim about not-being across kinds, which concerns otherness rather than a quality's reference to a subject (obs_theaetetus_0116, 160b-160c).

dispositions.label: safe_answer_formula
dispositions.reason: Three Phaedo passages mark the Form-based causal explanation as the safest answer, explicitly separating it from tempting but rejected accounts of how things become beautiful, large, or numbered. The epistemic function is methodological caution within a causal argument, distinct from passages that simply state participation as a cause (obs_phaedo_0195, 100d-100e; obs_phaedo_0198, 101a-101b; obs_phaedo_0200, 101c-101d).

dispositions.label: same_different_circles_cognitive_function

This cognitive function is distinct from geometrical mappings of visible and intelligible domains, where the line or cave supplies a diagram rather than a mechanism of judgment (obs_timaeus_0129, 44a-44b).

dispositions.label: same_other_assignment_to_motion

dispositions.label: soul_cosmic_range_and_form_participation

This structural scope contrasts with the kinship claim that identifies soul with the divine or intelligible by likeness of nature (obs_phaedrus_0117, 246a-246b; obs_phaedrus_0143, 248a-248b).

dispositions.label: soul_eide_divided

The schema's function is a copy-and-place distinction, distinct from the earlier three-term account that defines generation by source, receiver, and likeness relation (obs_timaeus_0193, 52a; obs_timaeus_0196, 52d).

dispositions.label: threefold_generation_schema

This is a generative relation among roles, distinct from the later compact inventory of form, space, and copy as already differentiated items (obs_timaeus_0186, 50d).

dispositions.label: time_as_moving_image_of_eternity
dispositions.reason: Timaeus 38a–38c defines time as a generated moving image of eternity ordered by number, linking cosmic motion to an eternal measure. The temporal-model role has a structural distinction from the intelligible living creature that serves as the Demiurge's paradigm for constructing the cosmos (obs_timaeus_0095, 38a-38c).

dispositions.label: two_paradigms_contrasted

dispositions.label: universal_pursuit_of_good

Universal desire here has a distinct function from the Form of the Good's causal or paradigmatic role, which explains how the good orders knowledge or reality (obs_republic_0244, 505d).

dispositions.label: affection_disclaimer_after_insult

dispositions.label: alcibiades_speech_reframed

dispositions.label: anticipated_laughter_preface

dispositions.label: argument_framed_as_divination

Its distinct role lies in the way the scene turns speech against its surface.

dispositions.label: argument_insight_presented_as_mockery
dispositions.reason: At Philebus 54d-54e, Socrates personifies the insight that pleasure is genesis as an agent who laughs both at pleasure-as-good and at delight in bodily replenishment (obs_philebus_0273 [54d-54e]). dispositions.label: charm_admission
dispositions.reason: At Republic 607c, Socrates asks Glaucon whether he too is charmed by poetry (obs_republic_0656 [607c]). The exchange acknowledges poetry's affective pull in both interlocutors and tests the force of that admission against the argument; it is not a forecast of hostile reception. The structural contrast lies in how the claim is staged.

dispositions.label: childish_wish_frame
dispositions.reason: At Sophist 249d-249e, the Stranger presents the proposal joining immobile and moved things under being as like a children's prayer (obs_sophist_0171 [249d-249e]). The image makes a tentative ontological proposal childlike and provisional, rather than insulating a speaker before challenge. This gives the scene a structural hinge between utterance and reception.

dispositions.label: comic_rebuke_marker
dispositions.reason: Four accepted records supply distinct comic signals: Glaucon calls an aporetic position laughable (obs_republic_0240 [505b]), reacts comically to Socrates' hyperbole (obs_republic_0261 [509c]), Socrates marks geometers' action-words as laughable (obs_republic_0313 [527a]), and Diotima laughs while exposing false consensus about Eros (obs_symposium_0099 [202b-202c]). dispositions.label: concession_to_the_many_hedged
dispositions.reason: At Laws 658e-659a, the Athenian concedes that music may be judged by pleasure only to restrict that pleasure immediately to the best and most educated, ultimately the most virtuous person (obs_laws_0177 [658e-659a]). dispositions.label: conditional_praise_of_claimed_art

dispositions.label: credibility_gap_exposed_by_behavior

dispositions.label: daimonion_evidence_claim

dispositions.label: deflection_from_self

The operation displaces explanatory responsibility, rather than simply stating an epistemic limit. The move has the function of changing the terms of the exchange.

dispositions.label: discourse_form_anxiety
dispositions.reason: At Theaetetus 169c-169d, Socrates worries that their speeches may take a childish form and attract a repeated reproach (obs_theaetetus_0174 [169c-169d]). Its function within the passage is to expose the gap between surface and uptake.

dispositions.label: ease_dismissal

dispositions.label: elenchus_as_demagoguery
dispositions.reason: At Gorgias 482c, Callicles recasts Socrates' questioning as youthful swagger and popular-orator demagoguery (obs_gorgias_0419 [482c]). dispositions.label: encomium_contract_disavowal
dispositions.reason: Four accepted records track different parts of the same encomium negotiation: Socrates contrasts truth-telling with appearance-maximizing praise (obs_symposium_0073 [198c-199c]), withdraws a promise to praise Eros sincerely (obs_symposium_0074 [198e-199b]), lets Phaedrus decide whether the speech counts as an encomium (obs_symposium_0158 [212c]), and disavows his ability to praise the men and city adequately (obs_timaeus_0015 [19d]). dispositions.label: etymology_style_characterized

The comparison is functional: it redirects attention from content to delivery.

dispositions.label: exemplary_first_choice_made_foolishly

This comparison belongs to the dialogue's staged contest over how to hear.

dispositions.label: explicit_accusation_of_evasion

dispositions.label: explicit_disavowal

This cluster groups a scene-level irony, not a general topic.

dispositions.label: explicit_doubt_signaled

The cluster's value is the recurrence of this reception-management move.

That cluster keeps the cited exchange tied to its dramatic setting.

This is a distinct shift in how the speaker positions the claim.

dispositions.label: in_text_accusation_of_mischief
dispositions.reason: At Lesser Hippias 373a-373c, Hippias says Socrates stirs arguments and does mischief, while Socrates replies that he does so unwillingly and asks pardon (obs_lesser-hippias_0088 [373a-373c]). The marker combines accusation with an involuntary-responsibility repair; it does not explicitly label the conduct ironic. The structural role is local: it controls what the audience is invited to hear.

dispositions.label: in_text_accusation_of_mockery
dispositions.reason: Two accepted records make mockery an in-text accusation: Callicles charges Socrates with verbal trickery and receives a counter-charge of feigned reluctance (obs_gorgias_0222 [496e-497a]), while Menexenus says Socrates habitually mocks the orators (obs_menexenus_0006 [235b-235c]). The shared operation is interpersonal attribution and counter-attribution of mockery, not a generic irony diagnosis detached from its target. Here the function is to mark a speaker's stance.

dispositions.label: interlocutor_infantilized_by_speaker
dispositions.reason: At Sophist 242c-242d, the Eleatic Stranger presents earlier ontologists as telling myths to the interlocutors as though they were children (obs_sophist_0149 [242c-242d]). The move assigns an infantile audience position to the present speakers; it is not a statement about the speaker's own knowledge. Its function is rhetorical placement within this exchange.

dispositions.label: interlocutor_praises_socrates_definition
dispositions.reason: At Gorgias 474e-475a, Polus praises Socrates for defining the fine through pleasure and the good immediately after Socrates has extracted the definition by rapid questioning (obs_gorgias_0109 [474e-475a]). The praise is a local response to an elenctic result, not Socrates' deferential posture before a test. The move has the function of changing the terms of the exchange.

dispositions.label: inverted_common_opinion
dispositions.reason: Two accepted Phaedrus records reverse the supposed political disdain for writing: ambitious politicians are described as eager writers who inscribe admirers (obs_phaedrus_0189 [257d-257e]), and writers are said to rejoice when texts survive rather than disdain them (obs_phaedrus_0320 [258b]). The operation overturns a common evaluation of speechwriting; it does not prepare a speaker against anticipated criticism. Its function within the passage is to expose the gap between surface and uptake.

dispositions.label: ironic_admiration_of_sophist
dispositions.reason: At Protagoras 315d-315e, Socrates eagerly wants to hear Prodicus and calls him exceedingly wise while admitting he cannot make out the speech from outside (obs_protagoras_0044 [315d-315e]). The mismatch between extravagant admiration and blocked access makes the praise ironic; it is not ordinary deference used procedurally. The comparison stays within the passage's ironic pressure.

dispositions.label: ironic_ascription_of_wisdom
dispositions.reason: Two accepted records use wisdom attribution for reversal: Socrates ascribes extraordinary wisdom to the eristic display (obs_euthydemus_0174 [300c-300d]), while calling Meletus apparently wise against the backdrop of Socrates' own ignorance (obs_euthyphro_0033 [2c-2d]). In each case, the evaluative attribution exposes its target rather than simply honoring an interlocutor. That comparison clarifies the scene's local reversal.

dispositions.label: ironic_characterization
dispositions.reason: Two Euthydemus records make understatement carry criticism: an argument is said to have more presentability than truth (obs_euthydemus_0206 [305e-306a]), and the brothers' extreme denial is called popular and mild (obs_euthydemus_0230 [303d]). The marker is ironic mismatch between surface characterization and argumentative reality, not deferential praise before examination. The comparison is functional: it redirects attention from content to delivery.

dispositions.label: ironic_praise_of_rhetorical_enchantment
dispositions.reason: At Menexenus 234c-235a, Socrates describes funeral oratory as enchanting its audience and embellishing qualities present or absent in the dead (obs_menexenus_0004 [234c-235a]). The elevated description exposes rhetoric as deceptive enchantment rather than truthful commemoration; it is not courtesy language licensing a test. This comparison belongs to the dialogue's staged contest over how to hear.

dispositions.label: ironic_self_deprecation_with_serious_point
dispositions.reason: At Gorgias 521b-521c, Socrates calls himself senseless for trusting he would escape prosecution, while the surrounding point is that anyone in Athens is vulnerable to prosecution (obs_gorgias_0374 [521b-521c]). The self-lowering is a vehicle for a serious civic claim, not merely a generic admission of deficiency. The cluster belongs to the dialogue's management of ironic speech.

dispositions.label: irony_suspected_by_speaker
dispositions.reason: At Cratylus 384c-384d, Socrates suspects that Cratylus mocks Hermogenes by denying that Hermogenes is his true name and linking the denial to his lack of wealth (obs_cratylus_0007 [384c-384d]). The marker is a speaker's inference about another's mockery; it is distinct from deferential praise or address.

dispositions.label: knowledge_disavowal_before_account
dispositions.reason: At Republic 506a-507a, Socrates refuses to speak as though he knows what he only thinks and distinguishes knowledge from report (obs_republic_0811 [506a-507a]). The marker is a methodological rule governing an account, not merely a free-standing confession of ignorance. This cluster groups a scene-level irony, not a general topic.

dispositions.label: knowledge_disavowal_before_critique
dispositions.reason: At Laws 635b-635d, the Athenian says he is not yet blaming the laws before firm examination and speaks from perplexity (obs_laws_1251 [635b-635d]). This is a procedural suspension of judgment before critique, not a generic statement that the speaker lacks knowledge. The cluster's value is the recurrence of this reception-management move.

dispositions.label: knowledge_disavowal_before_examination
dispositions.reason: At Gorgias 458d-458e, Socrates opens the examination by saying he may not understand Gorgias correctly even if Gorgias is right (obs_gorgias_0013 [458d-458e]). The uncertainty frames the coming questioning as a bounded inquiry, rather than a theatrical claim of ignorance detached from the object. That cluster keeps the cited exchange tied to its dramatic setting.

dispositions.label: knowledge_disavowal_deferral
dispositions.reason: At Sophist 232c-232e, the Stranger asks Theaetetus whether universal contradiction is possible, contrasts young and old perception, and defers judgment to the younger interlocutor (obs_sophist_0313 [232c-232e]). The marker is age-based deferral of a specific verdict, not an unqualified denial of knowledge. The exchange marks a distinct ironic move.

dispositions.label: knowledge_disavowal_enthusiasm
dispositions.reason: At Phaedrus 263d-263e, Socrates says enthusiasm has made him forget whether he defined eros at the start (obs_phaedrus_0198 [263d-263e]). The memory lapse is framed by inspired transport and follows rhetorical analysis, so its boundary is staged recollection failure rather than ordinary epistemic limitation. This is a distinct shift in how the speaker positions the claim.

dispositions.label: laughable_diairetic_result
dispositions.reason: At Statesman 266b-266c, the Stranger notes that the divisions have produced another laughable result (obs_statesman_0061 [266b-266c]); at 266c-266d he intensifies the image by making the king run with the herd (obs_statesman_0062 [266c-266d]). The comedy marks a failed classification and its absurd consequence, rather than serving as laughter to evade a live question. The cited moment is distinct in making stance part of the evidence.

dispositions.label: laughter_as_ironic_deflection
dispositions.reason: At Euthydemus 298e-299a, Ctesippus laughs, swears, and refuses to strike Dionysodorus, turning the demand about striking the dog into comic refusal (obs_euthydemus_0163 [298e-299a]). The laughter is an active escape from the sophistic trap; unlike general comic marking, it redirects the question instead of merely reacting to it. Its distinct role lies in the way the scene turns speech against its surface.

dispositions.label: luck_as_masking_device
dispositions.reason: At Timaeus 18e-19a, a manipulated lottery pairs citizens while rulers instruct them to attribute the outcome to chance so resentment will fall on fortune rather than design (obs_timaeus_0013 [18e-19a]). The operation is political concealment through staged luck, not protection of a speaker from anticipated criticism. Its structural work is to shape the exchange's pressure.

dispositions.label: method_called_ridiculous
dispositions.reason: At Cratylus 425c-425d, Socrates predicts that making things manifest by imitating them with letters and syllables will look ridiculous (obs_cratylus_0223 [425c-425d]). The ridicule targets the explanatory method itself and exposes its pretension; it is not a pre-emptive defense of the speaker's standing. The structural contrast lies in how the claim is staged.

dispositions.label: mock_admiration_for_rhetorical_artifice
dispositions.reason: At Phaedrus 273b-273c, Socrates praises Tisias' supposedly hidden rhetorical art in elevated terms while the method amounts to teaching how to make the worse appear better (obs_phaedrus_0237 [273b-273c]). The admiration is ironic evaluation through a mismatch between grand craft-language and manipulative content, not deferential staging before a test. This gives the scene a structural hinge between utterance and reception.

dispositions.label: mock_agreement_with_interlocutor_confidence
dispositions.reason: At Greater Hippias 286c-286e, Socrates agrees that defining the beautiful will be easy immediately after Hippias dismisses the task and after Socrates' own failure (obs_greater-hippias_0162 [286c-286e]). By echoing Hippias' confidence, Socrates turns easy agreement into a test of overconfidence; the marker operates through ironic mirroring, not reception management. The structural role is local: it controls what the audience is invited to hear.

dispositions.label: mock_astonishment_exclamation
dispositions.reason: At Lysis 208e-209a, Socrates answers Lysis' claim that his parents would beat him for touching their possessions with an emphatic Heracles exclamation and a leap to possible wrongdoing (obs_lysis_0036 [208e-209a]). The comic overreaction redirects a domestic claim into a mock accusation; it is neither a neutral surprise nor audience inoculation. Here the function is to mark a speaker's stance.

dispositions.label: mock_blessed_address
dispositions.reason: At Gorgias 512c-512d, Socrates calls Callicles blessed immediately before challenging his account of the good (obs_gorgias_0320 [512c-512d]). The honorific is a pointed address that carries the interlocutor into examination, not a general courtesy formula detached from the question. Its function is rhetorical placement within this exchange.
